transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (Nebula Head of Platform), Sofia Martinez (Nebula SRE), Dr. Amir Qureshi (CTO), Mei Tan (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot stability signals, runbook adjustments for cutover, and a planned chaos/chaotic-recovery rehearsal. Agreed to tighten canary thresholds, run targeted node-kill + network partition tests, and publish updated runbook and telemetry artifacts. Decided that rollback timeboxes will be explicit and that we'll exercise the fallback to the smaller quantized model as a degradation path.

Topics discussed:
- Canary thresholds (p50/p95/p99) and error budget gating
- Autoscale behavior under token-burst workloads
- Circuit-breaker and fallback routing to quantized model variant
- Chaos rehearsal plan: node kill, AZ outage sim, cache warm/cold scenarios
- Post-cutover on-call rota and alerting

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: All right hi everyone, thanks for joining. we'll give folks a few more seconds but wanted to get started so we don't run over. audio okay?
[00:07] Jordan: Yep, can hear you. Sofia too. good morning from our side.
[00:11] Priya: Morning. quick agenda: stability signals, runbook tweaks, and the chaos rehearsal plan. we'll go through recent telemetry and then pick thresholds.
[00:20] Amir: Sounds good. main ask from Nebula — low risk go-live. we want a clear fallback and a timeline to abort, otherwise legal and ops won't greenlight.
[00:29] Alex: Right, noted. the runbook will include explicit abort windows. priya, can you share the current p99 numbers?
[00:34] Priya: Yeah, pulling up the dashboard — quick caveat the sampling had some noise last night because of the synthetic load. p50 around 80ms for our small request set, p95 at ~320ms, and p99 floats between 720 to 980ms depending on sequence length. the KV-cache hit helped in the morning run, but we had a cold-cache experiment that pushed p99 over a second.
[00:56] Sofia: That cold-cache spike is the one that worries us. our latency SLO is 500ms p99 for user-facing flows — anything above that needs immediate rollback.
[01:05] Priya: Understood. we can gate the canary on a p99 threshold at 450ms to be conservative and leave a small error budget. also recommend a separate gate for error-rate — 0.8% 5-min window.
[01:18] Jordan: 450ms p99 seems tight. would that mean we need to keep the small quantized model as fallback?
[01:24] Alex: Yes, the plan is fallback routing. if we breach p99 or error rate we shift X% traffic to the quantized variant and then evaluate. note that quality drops slightly with quantized variant but throughput and latency improve dramatically.
[01:37] Amir: Can we quantify 'quality drops slightly'? our compliance folks will want numbers.
[01:41] Priya: For our eval set we saw a mean ROUGE-ish score drop of ~2.5 points on longer sequences. for short prompts it's negligible. i'll attach the eval sheet after.
[01:50] Mei: Also to be explicit — does fallback require a model spin-up time? during the spike can we route instantly?
[01:55] Priya: We keep the quantized pool warm on standby in Dedicated mode — so routing is near-instant. there is a tiny cold-start for KV-cache priming but route swap is immediate.
[02:06] Sofia: Ok good. what about autoscale? last run we saw scale lag during a token burst, which correlated with increased p99.
[02:13] Priya: Right. our runtime uses continuous batching; autoscale is reactive but has a 45–60s ramp to add nodes. we recommend allowing a buffer of 30% headroom for the initial ramp and set a circuit-breaker to hold traffic at 20% of baseline while nodes add.
[02:27] Jordan: So the circuit-breaker is a traffic-shaping mechanism that gates traffic to preserve SLOs?
[02:31] Alex: Exactly. it's a safety net — if we see token-cost per second spike and p95/p99 cross thresholds we'll hold new sessions and only let warmed sessions through, while also shifting a percentage to the fallback model.
[02:43] Amir: For the chaos rehearsal, can we simulate an AZ flapping then? that's what keeps me up at night.
[02:48] Priya: Yes. plan is three phases: 1) node termination (kill one worker per pool), 2) network partition between control plane and a subset of nodes, and 3) cache cold start (flush prefix cache). each will be run in a controlled 90-minute window, measure telemetry, then recover.
[03:02] Mei: We'll want runbook steps that map to the incident commander actions, e.g., "IC: initiate fallback; SRE: throttle incoming traffic; SE: validate responses."
[03:10] Alex: i'll update the runbook to include IC playbook and exact commands. we'll also include links to the blue/green switch scripts in the doc. link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/nebulapilot
[03:20] Sofia: Can we add a checklist for smoke tests post-switch? last time a small auth header mismatch broke a downstream function.
[03:26] Priya: absolutely — preflight smoke tests: auth flow, top-10 prompts, token accounting check, and a small latency sweep. Pass/fail criteria will be in the doc.
[03:36] Jordan: On alerting — our PagerDuty has runbook hooks; can Redwood create an alert mapping so our on-call knows what to do?
[03:42] Alex: yes we'll create an alert matrix. and we can push a sample PD playbook mapping.
[03:47] Amir: Who is the go/no-go owner? i.e. who has the final say to abort during the window?
[03:52] Jordan: i'll be the business owner for go/no-go with final sign-off but will act only on SRE recommendation.
[03:58] Alex: good — note that the runbook will capture escalation flow: SRE -> Jordan -> CTO if needed.
[04:05] Priya: quick note on telemetry retention — for the chaos rehearsal we'll increase sampling to 100% for 30 minutes and retain the detailed traces for 72 hours. that should give us enough to analyze tail latencies.
[04:18] Sofia: perfect. and can we also capture token-level cost spikes? want to see cost per 10k tokens during the test.
[04:24] Priya: yes we'll include cost telemetry and per-model unit token accounting.
[04:28] Mei: about rollback timeboxes — what's the proposed timeline? 15 minutes? 30?
[04:33] Alex: propose a 20-minute timebox from detection to decision for soft rollback (traffic shift to fallback), and a 45-minute hard abort to full cutover if signals don't improve. we can tune these values based on rehearsal.
[04:45] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. can you add the decision checklist so it's not ad-hoc?
[04:49] Priya: yep — checklist will include: signification of p99 exceedance over X minutes, error-rate threshold, degradation of quality above threshold, and unsuccessful recovery after Y minutes.
[04:58] Alex: let's walk through one hypothetical: AZ outage hits, p99 jumps to 1.2s, error-rate 1.6% sustained for 2 minutes. what's next?
[05:07] Priya: Trigger circuit-breaker, shift 40% to quantized model, hold new sessions, alert SRE and IC. if after 10 minutes p99 is still >600ms then move to 80% fallback. if still no recovery after 20 minutes then abort and rollback to previous deployment.
[05:26] Mei: when you say "shift 40%" is that global or per-route?
[05:30] Alex: per-route by default, but we can scope to only critical routes. for exploratory we can do global.
[05:35] Sofia: do we have metrics on quality vs fallback percentage? to decide 40% vs 80%...
[05:40] Priya: we ran a graduated ramp in the lab — 25% fallback had negligible quality effect, 50% showed small degradation on long-form summarization. i can share the matrix.
[05:50] Jordan: please. also, any thoughts on issuing a short user-facing message during the window? our product manager wants to avoid user panic.
[05:57] Amir: agreed, we should have a template message and a threshold to trigger it. maybe after hard abort only.
[06:03] Alex: we'll add a communication playbook — short message template and timing.
[06:07] Priya: one more item — storage latency. during one of our runs we saw increased S3 latency which affected model loading. recommend we add S3 latency gating to the preflight checks.
[06:18] Mei: good call. i'll add S3 and DB health checks to the smoke list.
[06:22] Jordan: what's the plan for the rehearsal timeline?
[06:24] Priya: propose 2027-06-15 16:00 UTC for the 90-minute rehearsal. Alex will update runbook by Friday and we'll circulate.
[06:33] Sofia: i'm available then. Jordan?
[06:35] Jordan: yes.
[06:36] Amir: ok for me as well.
[06:38] Alex: great. let's talk about observability — what panels do you want on the joint dashboard?
[06:43] Sofia: p50/p95/p99 token latency; error-rate per minute; fallback traffic percentage; model-quality samples (small daily batch); cost per 10k tokens; KV-cache hit rate.
[06:54] Priya: we'll expose those. also add per-AZ node counts and CPU/GPU utilization.
[07:00] Mei: and a link to the runbook in the dashboard header so IC can open from alerts.
[07:04] Alex: done.
[07:06] Jordan: i want to call out one risk — third-party tokenization library caused a mismatch in one downstream flow. can we pin versions?
[07:12] Priya: yes, we'll list pinned libs and a minimal reproducible test as part of the smoke.
[07:18] Amir: any mention of compliance logs and retention? legal asked for 90-day audit logs for inference metadata.
[07:23] Alex: Redwood supports configurable audit retention. we'll send the security/compliance doc and link it in runbook.
[07:28] Jordan: perfect.
[07:30] (brief cross-talk)
[07:35] Alex: ok last part — can we recap next steps? i'll list them then open for any additions.
[07:40] Jordan: go ahead.
[07:41] Alex: action items — update runbook with IC commands, schedule chaos rehearsal for 2027-06-15, Priya to run the chaos matrix and share telemetry, Nebula to sign off on thresholds by 2027-06-14, Mei to prepare blue-green scripts and smoke checklist. anything else?
[07:56] Sofia: add PD mapping.
[07:58] Alex: noted.
[07:59] Amir: and include the fallback quality numbers in the doc.
[08:03] Priya: will attach eval metrics.
[08:06] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook link and a calendar invite for rehearsal.
[08:11] Jordan: thanks team.
[08:13] meeting end.
